A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for a class of systems with a particular spatial structure, it is possible to solve the moving horizon estimation problem in a computationally efficient manner.
we have developed two distributed moving horizon estimation algorithms for a class of linear system chains, which have been analyzed in terms of computational and information overheads.

the computational overhead for moving horizon state estimation is reduced significantly by exploiting the structure in the state dynamics, and the computational complexity of the algorithm is reduced further if a sub optimal solution is acceptable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spatial structure of the system dynamics and the measurements can be exploited to design computationally tractable distributed state estimators for large scale systems.

the computational and information dependency overhead associated with solving a quadratic program for moving horizon estimation can be significantly reduced by exploiting the structure of the network dynamics.
for linear systems with bidirectional coupling, the computational overhead of solving the quadratic program is reduced to that of solving a set of decoupled Riccati equations.
